events.credibility_reason: Specific unanswered error identified by Mozhui–Dwary–Krishna (2025): A contains W′5, L(W′5) is non-word-representable (their Theorem 2.2), and L(W′5) is an induced subgraph of L(A), so L(A) cannot be word-representable. The containment/heredity step is sound; no reply or rebuttal from the 2021 authors in five years.
Appears to carry the same L(A) claim as arXiv:2108.02363, which is refuted by the specific unanswered 2025 critique; dissertation content itself unread.

why: The statement asks whether L(G) is always non-word-representable for non-word-representable G, so a single non-word-representable G with word-representable L(G) answers it in full: the 2025 Mozhui–Dwary–Krishna preprint is scope whole. Its non-word-representability premise rests on Kitaev–Pyatkin (journal-published), and the word-representability of L(μ(C5)) is certified by an explicit semi-transitive orientation of a 20-vertex graph, a decisive mechanical check, so I answered checkable rather than unreviewed. The close call was this: nobody, including the researcher, has actually run that check. The 2021 Akbar–Akrobotu–Brewer counterexample is knocked down by a specific, sound-in-structure, unanswered critique (W′5 ⊂ A plus heredity). Without that it would make the problem pre-snapshot resolved. The 2011 origin paper proves the yes direction for infinite families, so I scored it as case. Kitaev–Pyatkin 2024 does not concern line graphs (none). The two 2026 papers are about the reverse direction (variant). No AI involvement was found anywhere.
doubts: The researcher read Theorems 2.2 and 3.1 of arXiv:2509.03339 only through AI-summarised fetches, and nobody has publicly run the orientation check, so 'checkable' describes the object, not a check anyone has performed. If Theorem 2.2 were wrong, the 2021 knock-down would fail, though the 2021 orientation would still be unchecked. The thesis is dated only 'issued 2025', which is after the snapshot in any case.
